title: PMP in Plain English: Lead People, Deliver Work, Create Value
summary: Build a current July-2026 PMP mental model across People, Process and Business Environment.
plain_language_explanation: The current PMP exam tests scenario judgment across People, Process and Business Environment using predictive, adaptive/agile and hybrid approaches. The goal is not memorizing a single lifecycle; it is selecting actions that lead people, protect value and fit the context.

title: People Domain: Leadership, Conflict, Teams and Stakeholders
summary: Apply servant leadership, stakeholder engagement, conflict resolution, coaching and team performance reasoning.
body_outline: Adapt leadership style to team maturity and context.
Engage stakeholders continuously rather than only at approval gates.
Protect psychological safety and accountability together.
Coach teams toward outcomes rather than micromanaging tasks.
Use communication methods appropriate to stakeholder needs.

title: Process Domain: Scope, Schedule, Cost, Quality, Risk and Change
summary: Integrate delivery controls across predictive, agile and hybrid projects without treating one method as universally correct.
body_outline: Tailor lifecycle and controls to uncertainty and delivery context.
Integrate scope, schedule, cost, quality and resource decisions.
Treat risks as threats and opportunities with explicit ownership.
Use change control appropriate to the delivery model.
Make progress and quality visible through meaningful evidence.
Escalate only after understanding impact, ownership and available response options.

title: Business Environment, Benefits, AI, Sustainability and Value Delivery
summary: Connect project decisions to business outcomes, benefits realization, compliance, sustainability and responsible modern delivery.
architecture_notes: The 2026 PMP update increases emphasis on outcomes, value, business impact, AI, sustainability and stakeholder engagement. Project success therefore requires more than delivering scope: decisions should preserve strategic alignment, benefits, compliance and responsible use of technology.

title: Project Decision Evidence Pack
summary: Build a read-only project-health dossier before recommending governance or delivery changes.
steps: Identify project objective, value hypothesis and success measures.
Map key stakeholders, decision rights and unresolved conflicts.
Review delivery approach and tailoring rationale.
Review current risks, issues, changes, dependencies and quality evidence.
Compare actual outcomes to planned benefits and business constraints.
Draft options with impacts and owners; do not authorize change in the lab.

title: PMP Scenario Decision Tree: Diagnose Before Acting
summary: Use evidence-first reasoning for common exam and real-project scenarios.
diagnostic_order: Clarify the problem, impact and affected stakeholders before choosing an action.
Check whether the issue is people, process, risk, change, compliance or business-value driven.
Review the relevant plan, agreement, backlog, risk response or governance mechanism.
Collaborate with the closest responsible people before escalating unnecessarily.
Choose the least disruptive action that protects value and follows governance.
Escalate when authority, compliance, safety or material business impact requires it.

title: PMP 2026 Foundations Assessment
summary: Scenario assessment across People, Process and Business Environment.

assessment_items.question: A stakeholder raises a new concern late in delivery. What comes first?
assessment_items.answer: Understand the concern, impact and stakeholder need before deciding whether a formal change, backlog adjustment or other response is appropriate.

assessment_items.question: Should every project use the same lifecycle?
assessment_items.answer: No. PMI expects fit-for-purpose predictive, adaptive/agile and hybrid approaches based on context and uncertainty.

assessment_items.question: Does delivering scope prove project success?
assessment_items.answer: No. Current PMI guidance emphasizes outcomes, value, business impact and benefits, not scope completion alone.

title: Senior PMP Interview: Judgment, Governance and Value
summary: Senior scenarios testing stakeholder leadership, delivery tailoring, risk/change governance and value reasoning.
